title: A Thorn for the Garden Again
premise: Edmund Sterling, a woman passing as the invisible ledger-keeper of the Guild of Impossible Things, guards the Thorn Gate that binds the Hollow King—a parasite wearing the true king's crown for two hundred years. When a dying cartographer presses her a map drawn in living blood, Edmund learns the gate is failing and that she herself is the last heir of the gate's original makers, her 'ordinary' memory an implanted lie. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and shadowed by Wren, a disgraced knight sworn to the false king yet doubting his oaths, Edmund must reclaim her stolen inheritance and reforge the binding from within. In the climax she chooses love over duty—unbinding the king by offering the Hollow King her own memories as ransom—and in the end the true king wakes, the guild burns its ledgers, and Edmund, half-remembering but wholly free, opens a garden where the gate once stood.
about_author: T. M. Ravensworth is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed estates before turning to fiction, and whose fascination with what records conceal shapes every page. They live in a coastal town with too many keys and write only after midnight.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Edmund Sterling's POV. In the guildhall's undercroft, Edmund balances accounts of traded years, bottled names, and one door that must never be opened. Her routine invisibility is her armor. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath meticulous order—the reader senses she is hiding from something larger than her employers.

chapters.title: A Stranger at Closing Time
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A bleeding stranger collapses into the guildhall at closing bell, pressing a blood-drawn map into Edmund's hands and whispering 'the heir keeps the gate' before dying. The guild's enforcers arrive minutes too late. Emotional beat: shock and guilt; Edmund realizes the man was looking for her specifically.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Omit
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with a brief interlude in the guildmaster's voice via intercepted correspondence. Edmund discovers pages razored from the guild's oldest ledger—all concerning the Sterling family and the Thorn Gate. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your own history has been edited.

chapters.title: The Knight Who Knocks Twice
chapters.summary: Wren's POV introduced. Sir Wren Calloway, oath-bound to the Hollow King, arrives ostensibly to investigate the stranger's death but privately hunts doubts about the crown he serves. He and Edmund circle each other with careful courtesy. Emotional beat: mutual recognition of fellow prisoners.

chapters.title: Blood Remembers Its Ink
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The map responds to Edmund's touch, its lines crawling toward a city she has never visited yet dreams of nightly. First flashback fracture: a garden, a woman's voice singing. Emotional beat: longing for a memory she cannot own.

chapters.title: The Guild Does Not Forgive Debt
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The guildmaster accuses Edmund of theft and sentences her to 'quieting'—the same memory-surgery that made her ordinary. She flees with the map and three stolen ledger pages. Emotional beat: terror transforming into defiance.

chapters.title: Roads That Argue Back
chapters.summary: Alternating Edmund and Wren POVs. Wren intercepts Edmund on the north road but lets her go—or so each believes they chose. An ambush by guild hunters forces uneasy alliance. Emotional beat: reluctant trust kindling between enemies.

chapters.title: The City of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They reach Vessamyre, a city where citizens sell decades of their lives to the crown for safety. Edmund sees the Hollow King's economy of theft laid bare. Emotional beat: horror at scale; compassion for the complicit.

chapters.title: An Audience with the Crown
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren presents Edmund as his captive to buy time, bringing her into the palace. Face to face with the Hollow King, Edmund feels the thing behind the royal eyes notice her bloodline. Emotional beat: icy recognition—she has been seen.

chapters.title: The Garden Under the Palace
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Following the map's final line, Edmund finds a walled garden beneath the palace: the original gatehouse, overgrown but alive. There the fractured memories return—the Sterlings were gardeners of the binding, not jailers. Emotional beat: grief and homecoming entwined.

chapters.title: Wren's Oath, Unraveling
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Interrogated about his failures, Wren recalls the day he swore fealty and the moment he first suspected the king was hollow. He lies to his superiors for the first time. Emotional beat: the costly first crack in a lifetime of duty.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Daughter
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. A dying archivist reveals the dead stranger was the last mapmaker, and that Edmund's mother bargained her daughter's memories to the guild to hide her from the Hollow King. Emotional beat: fury at the loving lie that shaped her life.

chapters.title: Thorns Take Root
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The gate begins failing early; thorn-light bleeds through Vessamyre's streets, and borrowed years rot out of their owners. The city turns on 'the keeper's get.' Emotional beat: escalating dread as time collapses.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Long Gallery
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren is ordered to deliver Edmund to the throne room; he refuses and is branded traitor. They escape through the palace's long gallery while portraits of every previous keeper watch them run. Emotional beat: loyalty chosen at the price of everything else.

chapters.title: What Duty Costs the Loving
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wounded and hiding in the undercity, Wren confesses his role in hunting the last keeper's family twenty years ago—he was there the night Edmund's mother died. Emotional beat: love tested against unforgivable truth.

chapters.title: The Rite of Unbinding
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In the buried garden, Edmund learns the unbinding requires a keeper's willing memories offered to the Hollow King as ransom—it feeds on recollection. She prepares to give up everything she has only just reclaimed. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; sacrifice embraced.

chapters.title: The Hollow Court Assembles
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs—guildmaster, palace steward, a Vessamyre child—as the Hollow King summons the court to witness the gate's collapse and consume the city's remaining years. Emotional beat: converging dread; the whole cast drawn into one room.

chapters.title: Crown of Thorns, Crown of Ash
chapters.summary: Edmund and Wren's alternating POV. Climax part one: they fight through the hollowed court to the throne. Wren publicly breaks his oath, naming the king a thief, and takes wounds meant for Edmund. Emotional beat: courage as public ruin.

chapters.title: The Price of Remembering
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Climax part two: at the gate, Edmund offers her memories to the Hollow King. It gorges on her past—her mother, the guild, Wren—and forgets, in its gluttony, how to hold the crown. The true king wakes weeping. Emotional beat: transcendence through loss.

chapters.title: Aftermath of a Living King
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. The restored King Aldous confronts two centuries of crimes committed in his name; the guild's ledgers are burned by the very clerks who kept them. Edmund wakes remembering almost nothing—but her hands still know the garden. Emotional beat: fragile, uncertain mercy.

chapters.title: A Knight Without a Crown to Serve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Pardoned by the new king but refusing rank, Wren comes to the ruined gatehouse seeking Edmund, unsure whether she can love a man she cannot remember wronging or wanting. She asks him to tell her their story from the beginning. Emotional beat: tender, earned hope.

chapters.title: Where the Gate Once Stood
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, coda. Spring returns to the buried garden, now opened to the city above. Edmund plants thorn roses over the sealed gate—not as a lock, but as a memorial—and writes the first honest ledger of her life. Emotional beat: peace; memory rebuilt by choice rather than inheritance.
